narrative.text: Nadia comes alone and after dark, which tells you everything before she speaks. She sets a reel of magnetic tape on the desk without preamble.

Martin Luka. Lead anchor, Ashenmere Herald. Intercepted from a courier this afternoon. He is accepting payment from Lucan Vael to run a sustained smear against your Finance Minister — inflation, mismanagement, dereliction. Vael's money, Luka's face, every household in Veltria. I brought it to you because what you do with it tells me something I need to know.

She said that last part deliberately. She is not here as a source — she is here as a test. She wants to see if I publish it, bury it, or use it. Whatever I do, she will write about it eventually. The tape is real. The question is what kind of Chancellor handles a real tape.

choices.text: Publish it. Arrest Luka. Let the story run.
Keep the tape. Turn Luka — feed Vael false information through his own anchor.
Give the tape back to Nadia. Let her decide what to do with it.

narrative.text: Luka is arrested by morning. The tape runs on three rival channels by noon. Vael issues a statement denying knowledge of the arrangement — a statement that convinces no one. The Finance Minister holds a press conference that afternoon and is asked nothing about inflation. Nadia publishes a piece calling it 'the fastest vindication in Veltrian broadcasting history.' She does not mention that she brought me the tape. She doesn't need to.
One morning on the air and his career is over. I'd like it noted that I brought you a tape, not a sentence.

choices.text: Luka arrested, Vael exposed, and Nadia's name kept off the story.

narrative.text: Luka receives the tape and a visitor from Krel's office on the same afternoon. The conversation is brief. He continues broadcasting. His coverage of the Finance Minister becomes, over the following weeks, strangely balanced. Vael's money keeps arriving; Luka keeps depositing it; Luka keeps saying nothing useful with it. Nadia notices the shift eventually. She doesn't publish anything. She files it away. That is more dangerous.
Luka's next eleven broadcasts are scrupulously fair to the Finance Ministry. His producer notices and asks why. Luka says he has 'matured'. The producer writes that down too.

choices.text: A turned anchor with Vael's money in one pocket and Krel's card in the other.

narrative.text: I slide it back across the desk. She looks at it for a moment, then picks it up. She stands and buttons her coat without another word. Three days later, the Herald runs a long investigation into Vael's media investments — not the tape, but everything around it. Luka is not named. Vael is. It is slower than an arrest and more permanent. Nadia does not thank me. She doesn't need to.
The Herald's investigation runs to three parts. Within a fortnight Vael's media group loses two advertising contracts and a board member. Luka keeps his job and never learns how close he came.

choices.text: The tape stays buried, Vael is exposed slowly, and Luka never finds out.
